# Wayback Reel — Full Technical & Agent Specification

## Overview
Wayback Reel (`wayback-to-video`) turns any website's Internet Archive history into a smooth H.264 `.mp4` time-lapse video inside the browser.

## Endpoints

### 1. `GET /fun/wayback-to-video/api/timeline?url={domain_or_url}`
Returns one verified `200 OK` `text/html` Wayback Machine snapshot per archived year (`1995`–present).

Example response:
```json
{
  "domain": "info.cern.ch",
  "lookupKey": "info.cern.ch",
  "count": 27,
  "snapshots": [
    {
      "year": 1997,
      "timestamp": "19970404065412",
      "dateLabel": "04 APR 1997",
      "isoDate": "1997-04-04",
      "originalUrl": "http://info.cern.ch:80/",
      "archiveUrl": "https://web.archive.org/web/19970404065412/http://info.cern.ch:80/",
      "iframeUrl": "https://web.archive.org/web/19970404065412if_/http://info.cern.ch:80/"
    }
  ]
}
```

### 2. `GET /fun/wayback-to-video/api/snapshot?timestamp={timestamp}&url={originalUrl}`
Returns a `1280x800` JPEG/PNG visual capture of `https://web.archive.org/web/{timestamp}if_/{originalUrl}` with CORS headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin`) suitable for HTML5 `<canvas>` and `ffmpeg.wasm` compositing.

## In-Browser Video Pipeline (`app.js`)
1. Pre-warms single-threaded `@ffmpeg/core` (`0.12.10`) in a same-origin module worker (no `SharedArrayBuffer` or `COEP: require-corp` lock-in).
2. Composites sequential `1280x720` JPEG frames (`f_%04d.jpg`) at `15 fps` with warm paper framing, browser chrome header, date stamp, hairline progress bar, and cubic-eased cross-dissolves.
3. Executes:
   `ffmpeg -framerate 15 -i f_%04d.jpg -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -crf 20 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart wayback_out.mp4`
4. Cleans up WebAssembly MEMFS files after each encode to avoid 32-bit heap exhaustion.

## WebMCP Tools (`navigator.modelContext`)
- `get_wayback_timeline({ url })`: Returns the JSON timeline of yearly Wayback snapshots without starting video encoding.
- `create_wayback_video({ url, secondsPerYear })`: Runs the full UI pipeline and returns `{ domain, years, durationSeconds, bytes, downloadUrl }`.
